record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does there exist a timelike geodesically complete, inextendible Lorentz manifold satisfying an energy condition and having a partial Cauchy surface that contains a trapped surface?

evidence.quote: Is there a timelike geodesically complete, inextendible Lorentz manifold satisfying an energy condition and having a partial Cauchy surface which contains a trapped surface?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth, time-oriented, connected Lorentzian manifold of dimension $n\ge 4$. Recall the following notions:

(i) $(M,g)$ is timelike geodesically complete if every inextendible timelike geodesic is defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$.

(ii) $(M,g)$ is inextendible if there is no isometric embedding of $(M,g)$ as a proper open subset of a strictly larger connected time-oriented Lorentzian manifold of the same dimension.

(iii) $(M,g)$ satisfies an energy condition (for instance, the null energy condition: $\mathrm{Ric}(k,k)\ge 0$ for every null vector $k$; one may also consider weak, strong, or dominant energy conditions).

(iv) A partial Cauchy surface in $(M,g)$ is a smooth, connected, spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subset M$ that is acausal and edgeless (equivalently, met by every inextendible causal curve at most once).

(v) A trapped surface is a smooth, closed (compact without boundary), spacelike, codimension-two submanifold $T\subset M$ whose two future-directed null mean curvature vectors are both past-pointing timelike; equivalently, the expansions of both families of future-directed null geodesics orthogonal to $T$ are everywhere negative.

Question: Does there exist a Lorentzian manifold $(M,g)$ that is simultaneously timelike geodesically complete, inextendible, satisfies an energy condition, and admits a partial Cauchy surface $\Sigma$ containing a trapped surface $T\subset\Sigma$?
artifact.status_search_result: A direct web search did not turn up a published resolution of this question. The Penrose singularity theorem yields null (not timelike) geodesic incompleteness from a trapped surface in a globally hyperbolic setting with a noncompact Cauchy surface, so it does not preclude such an example, and the question of whether timelike geodesic completeness is compatible with a trapped surface in an inextendible spacetime satisfying an energy condition appears to remain unresolved in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: Notes on Lorentzian causality (Galloway)
status_evidence.snippet: Penrose's singularity theorem: a globally hyperbolic spacetime with noncompact Cauchy surface, satisfying the null energy condition and containing a trapped surface is future null geodesically incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Existing singularity theorems force null (not timelike) incompleteness from a trapped surface, leaving the timelike-completeness version open.

status_evidence.title: Singularities in general relativity (Luk)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of singularity theorems and open problems in mathematical relativity, including questions about trapped surfaces and geodesic completeness.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys discuss the interplay of trapped surfaces and completeness without settling the specific question.
